mpRateNote: Monetary Policy Rate cut 250bps to 10.75% at the 30 September 2026 MPC (from 13.25%), the lowest in several years, as inflation eased back inside the BoZ target band. Prior path: 13.25% held at the August 2026 MPC (26 Aug); 25bps cut from 13.50% at the May 2026 MPC; 75bps cut from 14.25% on 11 Feb 2026. The 30 Sep decision coincided with the 10% copper-concentrate export duty taking effect and the start of IMF successor-programme talks.

trendAnalysis.direction: USD/ZMW market mid 20.6407 — 1.60% softer than the 6 Nov snapshot (20.3157) and the weakest kwacha print since the second quarter. BoZ official mid was 20.4666 on 15 Nov (buy 20.4416 / sell 20.4916); the offshore market mid is running ~0.85% above that fix, a much wider premium than early November, which points to offshore demand rather than a purely domestic move. Against the crosses the picture is mixed: the kwacha is firmer on sterling (-0.22% to 27.2985), the euro (-0.20% to 22.7713) and the rand (-1.64% to 1.2197), but softer on the pula (+2.91% to 1.4740) and the yuan (+0.64% to 3.0581). Dollar strength globally, not a broad kwacha sell-off, explains most of the move.

trendAnalysis.outlook: The kwacha has given back roughly a percentage point and a half against the dollar in the ten days since the 6 Nov snapshot. USD/ZMW moved from 20.3157 to 20.6407, taking out the 20.50 area the November note flagged as the next level, while sterling, euro and rand all cost fewer kwacha — the signature of a stronger dollar rather than a Zambia-specific shock. The er-api offshore mid (20.6407) is ~0.85% above the BoZ fix of 20.4666 (15 Nov), so part of the gap is a wider offshore premium rather than onshore trading. Fundamentals are unchanged and still supportive: record copper output, copper prices holding near highs, reserves close to US$5.5bn, a near-complete debt restructuring, the US$1.47bn IMF staff-level agreement and the Lobito corridor advancing. The offsets are dollar strength, month-start corporate demand, fuel import costs after the November fuel-price adjustments and a materially easier policy stance post the 30 September MPR cut to 10.75%. Watch 20.65 — a weekly close above it opens 20.90; a slip back under 20.40 would suggest the move was offshore-only and mean-reverts.
trendAnalysis.projection3m: USD/ZMW 20.10–21.20 range. Copper earnings and IMF programme inflows supportive; dollar strength, softer policy and fuel imports the main risks.
trendAnalysis.projection6m: USD/ZMW 19.40–21.20 range. Direction hinges on fiscal continuity, copper earnings through the Lobito/export-logistics build-out, the pace of further BoZ easing and the global dollar cycle.
